title: Routing policy safety linter and explainable fixes
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Build a Console-integrated routing policy linter that statically validates customer-authored routing policies and surfaces explainable fix suggestions. The linter should catch correctness issues (invalid region/tier names, impossible fallbacks), safety regressions (unbounded fallthrough to lower-tier costly models), and high-risk misconfigurations (missing rate-limits, cross-region privacy leakage). Alongside warnings/errors, the UI should offer stepwise, explainable fixes that customers can apply with a single click or view as diffs. This ticket covers the PM scope: acceptance criteria, UX flows, telemetry requirements, rollout plan, and coordination with Eng/Design for the first alpha (console-only) release.
acceptance_criteria: Static policy linter runs on save and on demand in Policy Editor and flags >=7 classes of issues with clear severity levels (error/warning/info)
Each flagged issue includes an auto-suggested fix or a human-readable remediation note; one-click apply for safe fixes in the editor
Policy Editor shows inline annotations with hover explanations and links to docs/playbook for complex fixes
Preview mode simulates routing outcomes for a selected sample workload and highlights any changes if suggested fixes are applied
Telemetry events emitted for linter run, issue counts by class, apply-fix actions, and preview simulations (privacy-safe, sample-keyed)
End-to-end tests and guardrail unit tests present in ENG repo and a basic e2e test in Console CI
Feature gated behind 'policy-safety-linter' feature flag and rollout plan documented for staged enablement
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff with Eng (Ravi Patel) and Design (Aisha Kapoor). Aligned on 1) rule taxonomy, 2) minimal inline UX, 3) telemetry surface.
2026-02-20: Product/Design spike - prototype annotations in Figma. Decision to support one-click safe fixes and view-as-diff for non-safe suggestions.
2026-02-27: Eng estimates backend linter core as 5 points (ENG-61240) and console integration as 3 points (ENG-61241). Added to cycle 2026-W10.
2026-03-03: First engineering PR (linter proto) opened. Observed false positives for region-ambiguous names; added a rule exception whitelist.
2026-03-05: PM review of initial UX: recommend showing cost impact estimate for fallthrough fixes and adding a ‘why this matters’ tooltip for each rule
decisions: Scope-first release will be console-only (no API lint) to reduce blast radius and iterate on UX
Linter will be deterministic and rule-based for first release (no ML-driven suggestions). Revisit ML-based suggestions in follow-up.
Safe-fix actions limited to idempotent transformations (typo fixes, missing tier defaults). Non-safe fixes are suggested as diffs requiring manual apply.
Telemetry will avoid PII; use policy-hash and sampled workspace ids for aggregated metrics
design_feedback: Aisha Kapoor: Inline annotations are good; add friction for destructive fixes by requiring user confirmation and showing estimated downstream effect
Aisha Kapoor: Advocate for colorblind-friendly severity colors and concise microcopy for the hover explanations
Sasha Rivera (UX researcher): Suggested a short overlay tour on first-run to explain linter severity and one-click fixes
engineering_notes: Ravi Patel: Backend linter implemented as standalone service to enable reuse by Private deployments later. See ENG-61240 for details.
Ravi Patel: Rule set authored in YAML; will be shipped with versioned rule bundles. Need migration story when rules change.
Triage: Add a policy-whitelist store to handle customer-specific constructs that are valid but non-standard
